newsitem.title: GERMANY: Foreign demand boosts German chemical industry - VCI.
newsitem.headline: Foreign demand boosts German chemical industry - VCI.

text.p: German chemical industry output rose 4.9 percent between January and May and should grow about four percent in 1997 if exports and domestic demand keep up, the German chemical industry group VCI said on Thursday.
In the five months from January to May, turnover in the German chemical sector grew 4.3 percent to 77.9 billion marks.
"I thought the figures were relatively positive for Germany, especially if you look at basic chemical prices," Christine Dienhart, chemicals analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich, said.

"There is a possibility that it could be a little too positive, as it seems too focused on Germany. A general overview of prices, including the U.S. and Japan, might have helped. But I think prices will be okay for a while."
Producer prices for chemicals fell 0.1 percent in the first five months of the year.
The VCI said in a statement: "In the course of the year to date, prices have risen slightly, but this does not mean a change in direction of a trend of falling prices since the middle of 1995."
Dienhart said: "It is still too early to tell what might happen to the price cycle. If prices in the United States decline we will feel the pressure in Europe."
One of the key messages from the report is that internal growth in the German market is very low, and exports are the main engines for growth in chemicals.
"This revival can be mostly attributed to foreign demand," the VCI said, adding the weak mark against the dollar and other major currencies also helped boost demand.
"The outlook for the economy is viewed as positive by the majority of chemical companies. These hopes are principally based on foreign business," the VCI said.
The chemical business should grow particularly strongly in the United States and this would lead to an accompanying demand for German chemical products, it said.
In the first quarter of the year, exports increased by 7.4 percent to 27.3 billion marks. The VCI said exports to the U.S. rose 22.7 percent, while exports to Britain grew 12.5 percent.

"All in all, German chemical exporters are expected to increase volumes rather than prices," the VCI said. German export prices rose only 0.5 percent in the first quarter, which means that the increase in the value of exports was based on volume, rather than on price.
On the domestic front, however, there were only patchy signs of a pick-up in demand.

More efficient production methods meant an increase in demand of around 10.1 percent for pre-production goods, but because of weakness in consumer demand, there was less upward impetus in the consumer chemicals division, which saw a fall of around 4.1 percent. Domestic turnover declined by 0.1 percent.

Employment in the sector continued to fall, as German chemical companies implemented restructuring programmes. Average monthly employment in the German chemical industry from January to May was 505,800, down 2.9 percent on the same period last year.
